entry.summary: Visa exemption for tourism, business trips, conferences or visiting family and friends, under 90 days.
entry.max_stay: Under 90 days; status can't be changed without leaving Japan
entry.pre_arrival: Visit Japan Web for immigration and customs pre-registration (optional but faster).
entry.other: Strict medicine rules: dexamphetamine, pseudoephedrine and any cannabis or CBD are banned; codeine, morphine or oxycodone need a Narcotic Certificate.

tourism.detail: Australians can normally receive a 90-day landing permission for a short non-remunerated visit.
tourism.next: Keep proof of onward travel, accommodation and funds available and confirm the granted period at entry.

meetings.route: Visa-exempt Temporary Visitor for short business activity
meetings.detail: Business liaison, negotiation, contract signing, market research, after-sales contact and publicity can fit when the traveller is not remunerated in Japan and does not operate an income-producing business.
meetings.next: Carry the Japanese invitation and keep delivery of services outside the visitor schedule.

conference.detail: Participation as an attendee at conferences, seminars and briefings is within the published temporary-visitor examples.
conference.next: If the organiser adds a lecture, workshop, performance or fee, have them reclassify the activity before travel.

unpaid-speaking.route: Mission confirmation under Temporary Visitor, or host-selected working status
unpaid-speaking.detail: Conference participation can fit Temporary Visitor status, but the published material does not create a blanket permission for every active lecture merely because no fee is paid. Reimbursements, promotion, repeated dates and service-like delivery can change the analysis.
unpaid-speaking.next: Give the Japanese mission the invitation, agenda, expenses and exact duties and obtain a written classification.

paid-speaking.route: Activity-matched working visa with Japanese host and usually a Certificate of Eligibility
paid-speaking.detail: A remunerated lecture, workshop or speaking tour is not covered by visa-free Temporary Visitor entry. The correct status depends on whether the engagement is academic, artistic, entertainment, research or professional service.
paid-speaking.next: Have one lead host map every venue, fee and duty to the correct status before the tour is announced.

book-launch.route: Temporary Visitor for rights and publisher meetings; confirmed working route for an active paid appearance
book-launch.detail: Publisher meetings and rights negotiations can stay in the business lane. A reading, workshop or launch fee needs classification, while imported stock and local retail should be handled by a Japanese publisher, distributor or bookseller.
book-launch.next: Separate rights, royalties, appearance fees, imported copies, giveaways and point-of-sale receipts in the host brief.

ai-teaching.route: Professor, Instructor, Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services or another host-selected working status
ai-teaching.detail: Paid university teaching, school instruction and company training do not share one status. A one-off unpaid academic contribution still needs the mission to confirm whether visitor participation is enough.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the university, school or company to classify the institution, audience, curriculum, payment and duration.

remote-work.detail: The published route permits up to six months of remote work for an overseas organisation or overseas clients, requires annual income of at least JPY10 million and medical insurance with at least JPY10 million treatment cover, and cannot be extended.
remote-work.next: Prepare income, contract and insurance evidence and keep Japanese clients, speaking fees and local employment outside this route.

entrepreneur.route: Startup preparation program where available, then Business Manager
entrepreneur.detail: A Temporary Visitor can conduct market research and negotiations but cannot operate the Japanese business. Local-government startup programs can support a preparation period before the founder qualifies for Business Manager status.
entrepreneur.next: Choose a participating city, confirm its startup plan criteria, then map the office, capital or staffing and management role.

trade.route: Temporary Visitor for liaison, negotiation, contracting and trade-fair attendance; operating status for local delivery
trade.detail: Sourcing, publicity, market research and negotiation can fit the visitor lane. Direct local sales, installation, service delivery or business operation require a separate commercial and immigration analysis; an ATA Carnet can support temporary professional equipment, samples and exhibition goods.
trade.next: Use a Japanese importer or seller for local transactions and list temporary equipment separately for Customs.

artist.route: Artist or Entertainer status selected by the Japanese promoter
artist.detail: Paid creative work and performance are outside Temporary Visitor status. Japan distinguishes artistic activity from public entertainment, so the program and venue matter.
artist.next: Have the promoter classify rehearsals, performances, workshops, merchandise and every payment before the Certificate of Eligibility process.

mixed-mission.route: Temporary Visitor for the clean attendance and negotiation segment, or one principal working status covering the actual delivery
mixed-mission.detail: A mixed itinerary can combine tourism, meetings, speaking, teaching, sales and overseas remote work, but one visitor label does not absorb the remunerated parts.
mixed-mission.next: Build a dated activity ledger and obtain mission advice on whether the whole trip must use the principal working status.

filming.route: Ask the Embassy of Japan, Yarralumla
filming.detail: No official statement on this activity was read. Easy entry isn't permission to work.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of Japan, Yarralumla which visa covers it, in writing.

research.route: Ask the Embassy of Japan, Yarralumla
research.detail: No official statement on this activity was read. Easy entry isn't permission to work.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of Japan, Yarralumla which visa covers it, in writing.

volunteering.detail: No official statement on this activity was read. Easy entry isn't permission to work.
volunteering.next: Ask the Embassy of Japan, Yarralumla which visa covers it, in writing.

laws.rule: Authorities can arrest and charge you if they find trace amounts of illegal drugs in your blood or urine.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Japanese family law, including divorce and child custody, differs from Australian law in several ways. For example, joint custody of a child after divorce has only been possible since 1 April 2026, following legislative changes passed in May 2024. When divorcing in Japan, parents may now choose between sole or shared custody of their child or children. If the parents can't agree on their own, Japanese courts can provide mediation to facilitate a decision, or, the court may issue a judgement. Parents who divorced before 1 April 2026 can apply to the Family Court of Japan to change an existing sole custody arrangement. The court will decide whether to change the arrangement based on the child'
laws.heading: Family law

laws.rule: Some employment agents may mislead and encourage foreigners to work in Japan without: the correct visa financial arrangements in place This could leave you open to exploitation and prosecution. Authorities have arrested Australians for working in the entertainment industry while in Japan on tourist visas. If you want to travel to Japan for work: check the true nature of the work offered get the correct visa before arriving in Japan get legal advice before signing any contract
laws.heading: Employment law

laws.rule: Police can stop you on the street, demand identification and search you and your belongings. If you're in a public place, police can seize: knives longer than 5.5cm, including blades and penknives firearms any other weapons or things you could use as weapons drugs any item they reasonably suspect you stole or have unlawfully If they find any of these items in your possession, it’s likely that police will detain you. If you're arrested, police can detain you for up to 23 days without charge, including for offences you might think are minor. Police might hold you for weeks or months while they investigate and undertake legal proceedings. The initial police interview could last several hours. P
laws.heading: Police powers

laws.rule: If you're visiting Japan as a tourist or for business on a short-term visa, you must always carry your passport. If you live in Japan, you must always carry your residence card. It's illegal to: buy or drink alcohol if you're under 20 years old drive with any alcohol in your bloodstream allow someone under the influence of alcohol to drive a vehicle in which you're a passenger The following activities are also illegal: importing or possessing firearms or other weapons without a permit smoking on the streets in some parts of Tokyo and other cities using UHF-CB radios (walkie-talkies) that don't meet Japanese standards, such as those purchased outside Japan resisting arrest or other actions th
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Penalties for serious crimes, such as murder, include the death penalty. Other sentences can include: heavy fines lengthy jail terms with hard labour deportation
laws.heading: Penalties

laws.rule: Japan has strict rules about bringing medication into the country. This affects both medication imports and medication you carry for personal use. There are 4 categories (PDF 250 KB) of medicine. These are: general narcotic psychotropic stimulants You may need a permit or certificate to take medication into Japan. This will depend on the medication's classification, name and quantity. Some medication is banned, including: the stimulant dexamphetamine, used to treat ADHD pseudoephedrine, found in some cold and flu tablets marijuana, including medicinal cannabis or CBD oil Authorities could detain you if you're found with them. For narcotic medications, including codeine, morphine and oxycodon
laws.heading: Medication

laws.rule: To drive in Japan, you must hold either: a valid Japanese driver's licence, or a valid International Driving Permit (IDP) and a current Australian driver's licence After 365 days, you need to get a Japanese licence. Get your IDP before leaving Australia.
laws.heading: Driving permit

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The Japanese currency is the Yen (JPY). No restrictions apply to bringing foreign currency in or out of the country. Declare all amounts more than JPY 1 million or equivalent, when you arrive or leave. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. Cash is preferred in many places, but cards are becoming more widely used, especially in major cities. Hotels accept major credit cards. Credit cards may not be widely accepted outside major cities, and tourist areas. Some ATMs at banks and convenience stores don't accept foreign cards. Ask your bank if your cards will work in Japan.
